study type: Cluster randomised cross-over trial (analysis of serious adverse events within the trial cohort)
exposure: Testing and treatment for sexually transmitted infections (primary intervention of the WANTAIM trial)
outcome: Emergency caesarean section (as a cause of maternal admission)
Pre-eclampsia (as a cause of maternal admission)
Malaria (as a cause of maternal admission)
cohort: The study participants were 4,532 antenatal women and their 4,409 newborns enrolled in the WANTAIM trial in Papua New Guinea.
finding: The study identified a high burden of perinatal deaths and maternal and newborn morbidity, along with potentially preventable causes and avoidable factors, among the cohort in Papua New Guinea.
mod_finding: Emergency caesarean sections accounted for 16% of maternal hospital admissions.
